newsitem.title: UK: UK's Brown sees tough sanctions against work-shy.
newsitem.headline: UK's Brown sees tough sanctions against work-shy.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown on Thursday promised tough sanctions against unemployed young people who refuse to take up any of the work or training options in the government's welfare-to-work programme.
Press reports have speculated that the work-shy could lose 60 percent of their welfare benefits, compared to the threat of a 40 percent cut under the previous Conservative administration.
Brown refused to be drawn but said the sanctions would be serious. "We will be tougher than perhaps people originally thought in this area," he told a news conference.

Education Secretary David Blunkett will make a statement to parliament on Thursday afternoon giving further details of the 3.15 billion stg welfare-to-work programme to get 250,000 under-25s off the dole and into work or training.

On plans to allocate 1.3 billion stg from the government's 5.2 billion stg windfall tax to capital investment in schools, Brown said schools and education authorities would have to meet tough targets for examination results and discipline to qualify for a share of the money.
